title: subject_srv.exe (PID 12528) present in memory at acquisition — active network listener on TCP 3262
observation: windows.netscan on /root/cases/SRL-2018-WKSTN/base-wkstn-01-memory.img returned 148 socket records. Multiple entries show Owner='subject_srv.ex' (Volatility3 truncates ImageFileName to 14 chars), PID=12528: TCPv4/TCPv6 LISTENING on local port 3262 (Created 2018-09-06 19:37:07 UTC), plus UDPv4/UDPv6 ephemeral sockets (Created 2018-09-06 19:37:06, 19:38:09, 19:38:10 UTC). All other process-tree plugins (windows.pslist, windows.pstree, windows.cmdline, windows.dlllist, windows.malfind) returned 0 records due to a PdbSignatureScanner kernel-symbol resolution failure on this image (instant ~530ms returns, no error string). correlate_evidence('subject_srv.exe', '/root/cases/SRL-2018-WKSTN/analysis') returned verdict='ERROR' because (a) memory-side pslist returned no records and (b) prefetch parsing failed — pyscca/libscca not installed.
interpretation: Per CLAUDE.md confidence mapping, CONFIRMED may only be asserted when correlate_evidence() returns CONFIRMED_RUNNING/CONFIRMED_HISTORICAL/MEMORY_ONLY. Here correlate_evidence returned ERROR (tooling failure, not a negative finding), so this is recorded as INFERRED. The underlying netscan record is itself direct Volatility3 tool output (not a behavioral inference) and strongly supports that subject_srv.exe (PID 12528) was running and actively listening on TCP 3262 at the moment of memory acquisition (2018-09-06, ~19:37-19:38 UTC). T08 (correlate_evidence CONFIRMED_RUNNING) and T09 (pslist returns subject_srv.exe with PID/PPID) are NOT satisfied this session due to the symbol-resolution and pyscca blockers documented below.

evidence_quotes.claim: subject_srv.exe (PID 12528) listening on TCP 3262 at memory acquisition

title: Established inbound connection 172.16.5.50:56722 -> 172.16.7.11:3262 (subject_srv.exe's listening port)
observation: windows.netscan record at offset 0x8702b325f810 shows Proto=TCPv4, LocalAddr=172.16.7.11, LocalPort=3262, ForeignAddr=172.16.5.50, ForeignPort=56722, State=ESTABLISHED, PID/Owner not resolved ('-'). Local port 3262 matches the LISTENING socket owned by subject_srv.ex (PID 12528, see prior finding).
interpretation: HYPOTHESIS: The ESTABLISHED session on port 3262 likely belongs to subject_srv.exe given the matching local port of its LISTENING socket, suggesting an active inbound connection from host 172.16.5.50 to the malicious/subject service at the time of acquisition. PID attribution for this socket could not be confirmed (Owner/PID fields are '-' in netscan output, and pslist/pstree are unavailable due to the symbol-resolution failure noted above). This is unconfirmed and requires further investigation (e.g., re-running with corrected ISF symbols to attribute the socket to a PID, and checking 172.16.5.50 for corroborating outbound connection records).

title: Repeated outbound connections from 172.16.7.11 to 172.16.4.10:8080 (possible C2/proxy beaconing)
observation: windows.netscan returned 6 distinct CLOSED TCPv4 connection records from LocalAddr=172.16.7.11 (this host) to ForeignAddr=172.16.4.10, ForeignPort=8080, on local ports 59511, 59703, 60001, 60085, 60117, 60167. PID/Owner are unresolved ('-') for all CLOSED entries.
interpretation: HYPOTHESIS: Repeated short-lived connections to a non-standard HTTP-alt port (8080) on 172.16.4.10 from a sequential range of ephemeral local ports is consistent with periodic C2 beaconing or proxied traffic, but no process attribution is available (pslist/cmdline plugins failed — see tooling-blocker finding) and 172.16.4.10 / port 8080 does not appear in the known IOC list (known_iocs/suspicious_patterns in prd.json: stun.exe, msedge.exe, pssdnsvc.exe, atmfd.dll, 172.15.1.20, 172.16.6.12 — none match). This requires further investigation before any CONFIRMED/INFERRED malicious attribution.

title: Tooling blockers prevent T08 (correlate_evidence) and T09 (pslist) satisfaction this session
observation: Two concurrent tooling failures observed this session on /root/cases/SRL-2018-WKSTN/base-wkstn-01-memory.img: (1) windows.pslist, windows.pstree, windows.cmdline, windows.dlllist, and windows.malfind all return total_records=0 with error=null in ~530ms (instant, not a 30s timeout) — consistent with a Volatility3 PdbSignatureScanner kernel-symbol resolution failure, the same class of issue documented for the SRL-2018-DC memory image. (2) correlate_evidence('subject_srv.exe', case_dir='/root/cases/SRL-2018-WKSTN/analysis') returned verdict='ERROR' with prefetch error 'pyscca (libscca) not installed. Install with: sudo apt install libscca-python3', and memory.present=false because pslist returned no records.
interpretation: HYPOTHESIS/gap note: detect_host_type classified this case as MEMORY_ONLY (only base-wkstn-01-memory.img present, no Amcache/Prefetch/MFT on disk), so amcache/prefetch/mft sources were correctly absent for correlate_evidence. The remaining blockers are: (a) install libscca-python3 to enable prefetch parsing (moot for this MEMORY_ONLY case but required by correlate_evidence's pipeline), and (b) resolve the PDB symbol issue for windows.pslist (per prior DC-case remediation: run a working symbol-resolving plugin to fetch the correct ISF for this image's Windows build, then retry pslist with corrected symbol table). Until (b) is resolved, T09 cannot be satisfied (pslist returns 0 records, not subject_srv.exe specifically) and T08 cannot return CONFIRMED_RUNNING.
